newsitem.title: USA: Clinton friend settles with Rose Law firm.
newsitem.headline: Clinton friend settles with Rose Law firm.

text.p: A former official of the U.S. Justice Department agreed Tuesday to repay $400,000 that he embezzled from the Little Rock law firm where he and First Lady Hillary Rodham Clinton had been partners.
Webster Hubbell resigned in 1994 as the third-ranking official in the Justice Department and later pleaded guilty to filing false expense accounts and overbilling clients at the Rose Law Firm.

"We think the settlement is as fair to the firm as possible, given that Mr. Hubbell's ability to pay may be limited," said Ron Clark, senior partner of the Rose Firm. Hubbell, a lawyer, was disbarred following his guilty plea.
A consent order filed in federal court in Little Rock Tuesday requires Hubbell to make regular payments to the Rose Firm upon his release from prison, which is expected in December.

For almost 20 years, Hubbell was a close friend and political counsellor to President Clinton as well as Mrs. Clinton's law partner. A former mayor of Little Rock, Hubbell once served as interim chief justice of the Arkansas Supreme Court under Clinton's patronage.
When Clinton moved from the Arkansas Governor's Mansion to the White House, he appointed Hubbell associate attorney general, the third-ranking position in the Justice Department.

Hubbell was charged with fraud and tax evasion by Whitewater special prosecutor Kenneth W. Starr, whose investigation of the Clinton's business affairs broadened to include those of several Clinton associates.
